description:
## Why

The `MessageEnd{message: Assistant.t()}` event ships a finalized assistant message structurally. Consumers that receive it (replay, persistence, debug dumps, tests) need the same `block_id` that streaming events carried, without re-deriving from list position.

## Shape

Add a `content_index :: non_neg_integer() | nil` field to:

- `OctoPi.AI.Content.Text`
- `OctoPi.AI.Content.Thinking`

(`OctoPi.AI.ToolCall` already has provider-assigned `id`, leave it alone.)

Decoders populate the field at block-construction time:

- `apps/octo_pi_ai_anthropic/lib/.../decoder.ex:248-258` — `build_content_item` takes `position` and stamps `content_index: position` on Text/Thinking variants.
- `apps/octo_pi_ai_openai/lib/.../decoder.ex:197, 223` — `Content.Text{}` / `Content.Thinking{}` constructors at `open_block` sites take `content_index: state.content_count`.

## Acceptance

- Every `Content.Text` / `Content.Thinking` in a `Decoder.message/1` or `MessageEnd.message` snapshot has `content_index` set, matching the `block_id` carried by the per-block events from `.6`.
- Decoder unit tests assert `content_index` on the finalized message content.

## Tests

- Anthropic: a multi-block stream (text, thinking, text) finalizes with `content_index: 0, 1, 2` on the three blocks.
- OpenAI: same.

## Out of scope

- The agent-event redesign (`.6` proper).
- Persistence format changes — the field is additive on existing structs and any serialization that picks `text`/`thinking` keys will ignore it harmlessly.
title: Stamp content_index onto Content.Text and Content.Thinking
